This suggests a potential role of Salicylic Acid in modulating keratinization and ammonia levels, which are key factors in the development of Seborrheic Dermatitis. The integration of these pathways implies that Salicylic Acid may influence skin homeostasis by affecting keratinocyte differentiation and ammonia metabolism, potentially contributing to the inflammatory and pruritic characteristics of the condition. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Salicylic Acid and Seborrheic Dermatitis, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
